context_tokens.description:
ContextTokens is the input of the last round that reported one: unlike the sums, it is how
much of the model's context window the conversation occupied when the turn ended.

alias.description: Alias is the operator-assigned name, empty when the key is unnamed.

alias_version.description: AliasVersion is the version a rename must cite; zero means no alias exists.

fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint is the legacy keys-page identity, computed under the
"client-key" purpose. It is retained so existing clients keep working.

key.description:
Key is the key's display mask (`security.MaskSecret`), and the key itself only
when the caller asked for it with `include_keys=true`: the key page joins this
list against the configuration document it edits, and it needs the value to do
that, while every other reader renders the mask. The field always carries the
same shape for the same key either way, so a reader that masks what it is given
reads both forms identically.

usage_fingerprint.description:
UsageFingerprint is the identity this key has in the usage records
(`usage_events.api_group_key`), computed under the "usage-api-key"
purpose. Only this value can be joined to a request record, so it is what
an alias is stored against and what the "view requests" action filters by.
Empty when the cipher is unavailable; an empty value must never be used as
an alias identity.

oldest_request_record_ms.description: OldestRequestRecordMS is the oldest request record still stored.

request_record_days.description:
RequestRecordDays and PayloadDays are in force now; zero keeps rows (a zero
payload horizon follows the request records). The console sets only the
first; the payload horizon follows the environment unless the API set it.

scheduled.description:
IsScheduled is false when no maintenance loop runs in this process (the
demonstration); the stored setting then has no effect here.

source.description: Source is "console" once the operator saved a retention, "environment" until then.

horizon_ms.description: HorizonMS is the published horizon: rows older than it are gone or going.

auto_vacuum.description:
AutoVacuum is "incremental" when retention hands freed pages back to the
filesystem; "none" means the file keeps its size until it is rebuilt.

flow.description:
Flow is "redirect" or "device", the shape the card has to render. CPA
reports the same value when a flow starts; this one lets the console
describe it before anything is started.

oauth_provider_entries.description:
OAuthProviderEntries carries each portal's own name and logo, so a plugin that
fronts several brands does not have to show one title and one mark for all.

omc_source_url.description:
OMCSourceURL and OMCSourceEnabled describe the one source this console
manages itself. It is not an entry of store_sources: the list holds what the
operator configured, and the managed source is present exactly when its switch
is on.

interactions.description: Interactions is vertex-only: native Vertex Interactions API routing.

auth_indexes.description:
AuthIndexes are the runtime auth indexes of every key the provider holds. A request
record names the index of the key that served it, which is the only sound way to credit
traffic to a provider: CPA labels a family's keys by the family alone.

behavior.description: Behavior is nil for a family with no request-behaviour switches.

upstream_name.description:
UpstreamName is the name the provider carries in CPA's own configuration,
recorded before a local custom name replaces it.

It is not a secret - it is a label the operator wrote in config.yaml - and it
is the only sound way to join a stored request record back to the provider
that served it: CPA labels the usage queue with "openai-compatible-<name>",
so once Name has been overridden by a custom name the original is
unrecoverable and the join could only be guessed. Only the
openai-compatibility family names its entries upstream, so this stays empty
for the positional families, which CPA labels by family instead.

website.description:
Website is the provider's own homepage. It is Oh My CPA management metadata
rather than a CPA configuration field - CPA has nowhere to put it - so it is
stored beside the display name and joined on the same positional id. Only an
absolute http/https URL is ever reported, because the list renders it as a
link.

options.description: Options is absent for a model with none of the advanced settings.

request_retry.description: RequestRetry is nil when the provider inherits the global retry count.

supports_error_rules.description: SupportsErrorRules is reported on reads and ignored on writes.

reset_grants.description:
ResetGrants lists Anthropic rate-limit reset grants beside the Claude
quota, display-only: claiming one spends an entitlement and is out of scope.

source_index.description:
SourceIndex names the row this draft was opened from. It keeps a rotated
key tied to its stored settings without sending the old credential back.

options.description:
Options is nil when the client does not edit the advanced settings, which
then stay as stored.

behavior.description: Behavior sets only the switches it names; nil leaves all of them as stored.

runtime_policy.description:
RuntimePolicy, when present, is authoritative for cooling, the retry count
and the error rules, and DisableCooling is ignored. A request without it
keeps the single-switch cooling edit and leaves retry and rules as stored,
so a client that never carried the policy cannot erase one.

test_model.description: TestModel is console metadata; nil preserves it, empty selects automatic.

website.description:
Website is operator metadata, not a CPA field. nil means "leave the stored
value alone"; a present empty string clears it. That distinction is what
lets a rename save from a client that never carried a website field avoid
erasing one.

credentials.description:
Null when the gateway could not be reached: a count that could not be read is
not zero credentials.

freelist_count.description:
FreelistCount and FreePageBytes describe pages inside the file that later writes
reuse. They are never presented as reclaimable disk space.

journal_mode.description:
JournalMode is observed, not assumed. WALMode is derived from it, which is why
the page can no longer claim a mode the database is not in.

synchronous.description:
Synchronous, ForeignKeys and BusyTimeoutMS are null when the connection did not
answer for them, rather than defaulted to a value nobody measured.

data_volumes.description: DataVolumes are record counts, so a size can be read against the data behind it.

maintenance.description:
Maintenance is the running or last maintenance job. It is served from memory,
so it stays readable while a job holds the database.

maintenance_admission.description: MaintenanceAdmission states what VACUUM would need, before it is run.

update_check_on_page_load.description:
UpdateCheckOnPageLoad tells the page whether it may check when it is opened. The server
answers this rather than the page guessing, because the switch exists precisely so an
operator can stop page visits from spending requests, and a page that checked anyway would
defeat it. The manual button is unaffected and always available.

checkpoint.description: Checkpoint is SQLite's own result row, null when it was never read.

incomplete.description:
Incomplete distinguishes "the statement ran" from "it did its job": SQLite does
not error when a checkpoint is blocked. IncompleteReason is a code the console
words: "reader_blocked" or "log_not_truncated".

job_id.description:
JobID identifies one admitted job for the life of the process, monotonically. A reader uses it
to tell a later job from an earlier one, which the start time cannot promise: it is the wall
clock, so two jobs can share a millisecond and a synchronised clock can step backwards.

attempted_at_ms.description:
AttemptedAtMS is when a check was last tried, successful or not, so the page can
say a failure is recent without pretending the data is.

checked_at_ms.description: CheckedAtMS is when the stored index was last read successfully.

notes_available.description:
NotesAvailable is false when this process holds no release notes, which is the
normal state after a restart.

range_complete.description: RangeComplete is false when the release walk stopped early.

running_version.description:
RunningVersion is what is running here; empty when the gateway never reported
one, which is different from a version that could not be parsed.

body.description:
Body is untrusted remote Markdown. The frontend renders it without raw HTML and
without loading remote images.

stargazers_count.description:
StargazersCount is null until a read has succeeded, which the link renders as
no count at all rather than as zero.

image.description:
Image is the configured image reference, shown so a pinned deployment can see
what it is pinned to.

api_key_alias.description:
APIKeyAlias is the operator-assigned name for the caller key, resolved
server-side from the fingerprint in APIGroupKey. It is a display label
only: APIGroupKey stays the filter identity, so renaming a key never
changes what a saved filter or a drill-down link selects. Empty when the
key has not been named.

api_key_mask.description:
APIKeyMask is the display-only label for the caller key. The request
record keeps only a fingerprint, so records ingested before the mask
column existed omit it.

fail_status_code.description:
FailStatusCode is the HTTP status a failed request ended with; absent when
CPA reported none. The error body stays on the single-record view.

provider_key_mask.description:
ProviderKeyMask is the display-only mask of the upstream credential that
answered the request, resolved at read time from the credential lists CPA
currently reports (see usage_provider_key_masks.go). It is empty whenever
the credential cannot be identified - a rotated or deleted key, an
unclaimed or ambiguously claimed index, an OAuth credential, or a gateway
that could not be read - in which case the console prints nothing rather
than a guess. A provider that is merely switched off is not one of those
cases: its current state does not change which key answered.

response_model.description:
ResponseModel is the model the upstream reported having served. Absent
when it reported none, which is not a claim that the request's model ran.

images.description: Images are references; the page reads each from the image endpoint.

has_usage.description:
HasUsage is whether the deployment has ever recorded a request. It is not a
count of request records: those roll out of retention while the usage they
described stays, so an empty record table does not mean an empty dashboard.

as_of_ms.description:
AsOfMS is the instant the window was evaluated; the next poll should
expect at least this much drift.

bucket_ms.description:
BucketMS is the grid step, so the UI can pace itself to the resolution it
is actually being served.

series_start_ms.description:
SeriesStartMS is the first bucket of the full grid. Anything the client
holds before it has slid out of the window.

tail_from_ms.description: TailFromMS is the first bucket this response carries.

cost_usd.description:
CostUSD is the group's priced spend at request-time prices. It is null
rather than zero when the group carried no priced request, so a client
can tell "unpriced" from "free" the way the cost tile already does.

folded.description:
Folded marks the aggregate group holding every model outside the top N. It is a
separate discriminator rather than a reserved display name: a deployment may
legitimately serve a model whose name collides with whatever label the group would
use, and a name-based test would then silently merge real traffic into the
remainder or split the remainder in two.

model.description:
Model is the group's key, meaningful only when Folded is false. In the
model view it is the upstream model name; in the call view it is the call
point: the client-requested alias, or the upstream model when no alias
was requested.

priced_requests.description:
PricedRequests is how many of the group's requests carried a price. The
panel surfaces it when it is lower than Requests, because a spend summed
over part of the traffic is not the spend of the whole.

series.description:
Series is the group's own token volume on the window's bucket grid, zero-filled so
every group spans the whole window. Without that a model that went quiet halfway
through would draw a line that stops, which reads as a gap in the data rather than
as a model that stopped being used.

models.description: Models is ranked by token volume, descending, with the folded group last.

partial_errors.description:
Errors reports what could not be read, so a panel can say its numbers are partial
rather than presenting a short list as the whole picture.

total_tokens.description:
TokenTotal is the window's own total, summed from the same rows the groups were
built from. It is deliberately not copied from the KPI tiles' response: the two
panels read on different cadences, so they can legitimately describe slightly
different instants, and borrowing the tiles' number would let the donut's centre
disagree with the slices around it.

bucket_ms.description:
BucketMS is the activity grid every row's buckets sit on. It is coarser than the window's
chart grid: the list draws one block per bucket in a narrow column, and the chart grid's
forty-eight would leave each block a sliver.

credentials.description:
Credentials is the traffic API keys answered, by each key's runtime auth index. A configured
provider is credited from here, through the indexes of its own keys, and never from a label:
CPA labels every key of a family, and that family's OAuth channel, the same.

providers.description:
Providers is the traffic of every record no API key answered, by the channel label CPA
wrote: OAuth channels, and records that name no credential.

cache_read.description:
CacheReadTokens and CostNanos are per-bucket, so the cache-rate and cost
tiles can plot their own series instead of repeating the token volume.
Nanos rather than a float keeps the wire value exact; the browser scales it.

from_ms.description:
FromMS and ToMS are the exact inclusive instant range a click opens in the request
list. For today the range stops at the read instant rather than at the following local
midnight, so the cell and the list it opens describe the same interval - a record
timestamped later today (an upstream clock running ahead) is in neither.

reasoning.description:
Reasoning and cache reads are the two components the window's own tiles print,
so a day can be decomposed the same way the tile above it is.

requests.description:
Requests and Failures let the readout interpret a spike without a second
request per day.

tokens.description:
Tokens is zero for a day with no stored record, which is what a day that has not happened
yet also is. The client does not distinguish the two: a future day is a day nothing is
stored for, and the panel shows both as "no record" rather than inventing a pending state
that has no meaning to a reader comparing days.

as_of_ms.description: AsOfMS is the instant the grid was resolved against, on the viewer's calendar.

days.description:
Days is the whole grid, oldest first, one entry per calendar day. Days with no traffic
are present with zero totals, and so are the days of the current week that have not
happened: the grid's shape is its span, and the client should not have to reconstruct
which days were missing.

first_stored_ms.description:
FirstStoredMS is the earliest retained usage fact for this instance, or null
when none has been captured. Days before it have no stored usage - which is a
statement about storage, not about whether the gateway was running. The panel
labels those cells accordingly rather than claiming nothing happened.

timezone.description:
Timezone is the IANA zone the days were built in, echoed so a response and the
strip it was rendered into cannot silently disagree about where a day starts.

open_end.description:
OpenEnd marks a range whose end tracks the current time (the picker's
open-ended "through now" mode). The client polls those the same way it
polls a relative preset.

expected_request_record_days.description:
ExpectedRequestRecordDays is the horizon the console confirmed against. The
write is refused when another console has replaced it since.

compare_window.description: Compare is the period the window is measured against; null for all time.

previous_rows.description:
PreviousRows are the comparison period's per-bucket totals per dimension tuple,
carrying the same columns as Rows so the client can compute outlier-robust baselines
under arbitrary dimension filters.

is_client_key.description:
IsClientKey is false for traffic that reached CPA without a client key,
which CPA labels with a provider or endpoint instead of a fingerprint.

weekday.description: Weekday counts from Monday (0) to Sunday (6).

cells.description: Cells hold all 168 weekday-hour slots, Monday first, zero where nothing ran.

open_end.description:
OpenEnd marks a window whose end follows the clock: a sliding preset, the
current calendar unit, or an open custom range. Only those are polled.

to.description: ToMS is inclusive, like the dashboard's.

widened.description:
Widened reports that request records behind the retention horizon could not
split an edge bucket, so the window read was widened to whole fact buckets.

remember.description: Remember asks for the long session ("keep me signed in"). The key itself is never kept.

display_name.description:
DisplayName is the operator's own name for the credential, kept by Oh My
CPA rather than CPA; DisplayNameVersion is what a rename must quote back.

model_aliases.description:
ModelAliases are the credential's own aliases, resolved before its
provider's OAuth aliases.

openapi.description:
OpenAPI is nil while a Vertex service account leaves the partner-model
route to CPA's model-name detection; false is an explicit opt-out.

openapi_legacy_models.description:
OpenAPILegacyModels are names CPA also registers from the credential's
`models` key. The console never writes that key, so they are reported
rather than edited: removing a name from OpenAPIModels does not remove it.

openapi_location.description: OpenAPILocation overrides the credential's location for that route only.

request_retry.description: RequestRetry is nil when the credential inherits the retry count.

request_scoped_errors.description:
ErrorRules are the credential's own request-scoped error rules, which
replace its channel's while the list is not empty.

api_keys.description:
APIKeys is how many of Count are the runtime entries CPA lists for its
`{family}-api-key` configuration rather than auth files, and
APIKeysDisabled how many of those are disabled. CPA files both under the
family's type, so without the split a Codex OAuth channel would count every
configured Codex API key as one of its own credentials.

disabled.description:
Disabled is how many of Count the gateway currently reports disabled. A
surface needs it to tell a channel switched off wholesale from one whose
remaining credentials still serve, which the total alone cannot say.

expected_auth_index.description:
ExpectedAuthIndex and ExpectedName are optional preconditions. Providers
are addressed positionally, and the client now retries a transient failure,
so between two attempts another session could delete a provider and shift
every later index. Without a precondition that retry would toggle a
different provider than the operator clicked, silently. When either is
supplied it must still match the entry at that index, or the write is
refused with a conflict instead of touching the wrong row.

They are optional rather than required so an older client keeps working;
the browser always sends whichever of the two its row carries.

candidate.description:
Candidate is an OpenRouter model a custom or linked price could follow
that the operator has not seen yet.

interactions.description:
Interactions selects the Interactions dialect for a vertex draft whose
stored entry has not been read; stored entries resolve it server-side.

models.description: Models lists, per member key, the model names a client can request from it.

unknown.description: Unknown names the members whose models could not be read.

api_key_alias.description:
APIKeyAlias is the operator-assigned name for the caller key, resolved
server-side from the fingerprint in APIGroupKey. It is a display label
only: APIGroupKey stays the filter identity, so renaming a key never
changes what a saved filter or a drill-down link selects. Empty when the
key has not been named.

api_key_mask.description:
APIKeyMask is the display-only label for the caller key. The request
record keeps only a fingerprint, so records ingested before the mask
column existed omit it.

fail_status_code.description:
FailStatusCode is the HTTP status a failed request ended with; absent when
CPA reported none. The error body stays on the single-record view.

provider_key_mask.description:
ProviderKeyMask is the display-only mask of the upstream credential that
answered the request, resolved at read time from the credential lists CPA
currently reports (see usage_provider_key_masks.go). It is empty whenever
the credential cannot be identified - a rotated or deleted key, an
unclaimed or ambiguously claimed index, an OAuth credential, or a gateway
that could not be read - in which case the console prints nothing rather
than a guess. A provider that is merely switched off is not one of those
cases: its current state does not change which key answered.

response_model.description:
ResponseModel is the model the upstream reported having served. Absent
when it reported none, which is not a claim that the request's model ran.

records.description:
Records are attempts, newest first, projected exactly as the request list
projects them, so the panel names a model and a credential the way the
list does.

id.description:
ID is the OpenAI-compatible identifier. CPA advertises client-visible
call points under this field, so CallPoint is an explicit alias for the
surface that must select by call point rather than by an upstream name.

auth_rejected.description:
AuthRejected marks that CPA refused the management key, which the UI must
present as a configuration problem rather than a transient one.

captured.description: Captured counts records persisted to the inbox by this pass.

decode_incomplete.description:
DecodeIncomplete marks that rows were still pending when the decode wait
expired; the background loop keeps working on them.

decoded.description:
Decoded counts processed inbox rows within this pass's capture bounds,
including rows decoded before the persistence barrier began.

enabled.description: Enabled is false when this deployment runs no collector at all.

error.description: Error is why the request was not served. Empty only on success.

failed.description:
Failed counts records from this pass whose payload could not be decoded.
They leave no event behind, so a sync that dropped records is not a sync.

mode.description: Mode is the transport that served the pass.

pending.description:
Pending is how many records from this pass were still awaiting decoding
when the wait ended.

synced.description:
Synced is true only when a pass drained everything it found and every
record it captured reached usage_events.

auth_rejected.description:
AuthRejected marks that the failure in force is CPA refusing the key, which
the UI should surface as an actionable configuration error.

failing.description:
Failing is true from a failed collection attempt until a pass next
succeeds. LastError is history and stays after recovery, so it cannot
answer "is collection working now"; this does.

const.description: Const is *any because a JSON null (Go nil) is a valid value.

weight.description: Weight nil clears the key's own weight, so CPA runs it as 1.

reset_grants.description:
ResetGrants lists Anthropic rate-limit reset grants beside the Claude
quota, display-only: claiming one spends an entitlement and is out of scope.

id.description: ID is the upstream key; the console names known ones.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO 4217 code of the amounts above; empty means USD.

auto_renews.description:
IsAutoRenewing reports whether upstream says the plan will renew. Nil when
the source does not expose it.

balances.description: Balances are dollar allowances outside the plan's windows.

credits.description:
Credits is the account's prepaid credit standing. Nil when the provider
reports none.

expires_source.description:
ExpiresSource names where ExpiresAtMS came from; see the PlanSource
constants. Empty on snapshots written before provenance was tracked.

metrics.description:
Metrics are the figures a plugin publishes beside its windows (its quota
summary), in the order it lists them.

usage_breakdown.description: UsageBreakdown splits the plan's shared usage by product.

description.description:
Description is the provider's own words for the window's standing, such as
"183 / 2,000 credits left". A plugin bucket publishes its amounts only here,
so it is the one figure a plugin window has beside its percentage.

usage.description:
Usage and estimated full-window capacity are read-time projections. Upstream
percentages and reset times remain the authority for quota availability.

last_used_ms.description:
LastUsedMS is the newest request time observed in the window, which is the
same clock the request list prints.

max_input.description:
MaxInput is the largest prompt sampled, which tells the editor whether a
long-context tier is ever reached.

alias.description:
Alias is the operator-assigned name for a key-shaped facet, filled in by the
API layer from the same fingerprint as Value. It is not read from a column,
because a name is stored once per key rather than once per record.

model_aliases.description:
AuthTypes, ReasoningEfforts and ServiceTiers are closed vocabularies CPA
reports, which is exactly what a dropdown is for. ModelAliases is the same
shape: a client-requested alias is a short label with few distinct values,
and it is a filter dimension, so it needs a dropdown rather than a text box
whose edits would have to guess at exact matching. Endpoint and UserAgent are
deliberately absent: both are long free-form values where a typed substring
beats a 200-row list, and the endpoint URL must never be handed to the
browser (the list projection drops it for the same reason).

oauth_provider.description:
OAuthProvider is the login portal that issued the credential, for a plugin that declares
several; a surface cannot draw the credential's brand without it.

BearerAuth.description: Bearer CPA management key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`) accepted by capability, MCP, and management endpoints.
BearerAuth.name: Authorization

CookieAuth.description: Console session cookie issued by POST /api/auth/login (plus same-origin check on state-changing requests).
CookieAuth.name: Cookie
